items.text: Non-API uploads run in shared Scheduler::Defer.later queue, so large uploads stall unrelated deferred work
The same 10MB constant is duplicated in multiple places, risking client/server limit drift
PR defines downsize method twice (lines 145-151) - a 4-arg and 3-arg version - but Ruby's last definition wins, making the 4-arg version dead code

API URL-download cap changed from max_image_size_kb to hardcoded 10 megabytes, ignoring site settings and causing larger API URL uploads to be truncated rather than cleanly rejected on sites with limits above 10 MB
Each upload can trigger up to 5 sequential ImageMagick plus ImageOptim runs on files up to 10 MB, with failing conversions retried until attempts run out due to ignored return value

The downsize loop only shrinks to ~33% of the original after 5 iterations (0.8^5), so a 10MB image may still exceed max_image_size_kb and proceed to Upload.create_for despite the comment promising automatic reduction
If OptimizedImage.downsize fails and returns false, the loop keeps retrying and the oversized file continues

The method `self.downsize` is defined twice in optimized_image.rb. Ruby has no overloading, so the second definition replaces the first, causing every caller using the old 5-argument form (like ResizeEmoji job) to raise ArgumentError
API URL download cap changes from max_image_size_kb to hardcoded 10.megabytes, ignoring site settings and causing files over 10 MB to be truncated instead of rejected
The hardcoded 10MB limit for images likely shouldn't apply to attachment uploads
The loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size
tempfile.size in Ruby won't reflect updated size after OptimizedImage.downsize because Ruby caches the file size - need to reopen or stat the file to get actual new size
Code calling downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) will fail because Ruby will try to match the 3-argument signature instead
Hardcoded max size of 10 MB loses per-type flexibility - previous logic likely resolved max size dynamically based on type (image vs attachment)
ResizeEmoji job at app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 calls OptimizedImage.downsize with 5 arguments but the redefined method only takes 3-4 arguments, breaking custom emoji resizing

With allow_animated_thumbnails enabled, downsize_instructions_animated runs gifsicle with --resize-fit 80% but --resize-fit expects WxH geometry, causing gifsicle to exit non-zero and burn all 5 retry attempts before rejecting the upload
Second `downsize` definition overrides the width/height version, so existing callers that pass separate max width and height will start raising `ArgumentError`
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.
No tests cover the new downsize loop, changed OptimizedImage.downsize/optimize signatures, or client validation change

Existing caller in app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 calls OptimizedImage.downsize with 5 arguments, which will raise ArgumentError at runtime since only the 3-4 arg version survives, breaking emoji resizing

The new `downsize` overload passes the `dimensions` string directly through to `gifsicle --resize-fit` for animated GIFs, but gifsicle only accepts pixel-based `WxH` geometry and does not support percentage strings, creating inconsistency where downsizing animated GIFs with percentage geometry will fail while static images succeed

Client-side upload size check replaces dynamic site settings with hardcoded 10*1024 KB limit, causing attachments between max_attachment_size_kb and 10 MB to pass browser validation but get rejected by server

API URL-based uploads are downloaded with a fixed 10MB limit (FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)), ignoring configured upload limits, preventing API clients from uploading via URL when instance allows >10MB and downloading more than allowed for smaller configured limits
HTTP 413 handler always tells user the limit is 10240 KB regardless of actual nginx client_max_body_size setting

Hardcoded 10MB limit on line 182 replaces dynamic max_attachment_size_kb setting, causing non-image attachments to pass client validation but fail server-side when they exceed the admin-configured limit but are under 10MB
Using the same path for input and output in image processing is risky - if the operation fails mid-write, the original file is lost
Using a fixed 10.megabytes download cap ignores SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb and can cause instance configuration to be bypassed or prevent larger configured limits

Client-side upload validation hard-codes maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 for both images and attachments, ignoring configured SiteSetting limits, which blocks uploads when site allows >10MB and allows oversized files to start uploading only to be rejected server-side

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
With allow_animated_thumbnails off, convert file[0] writes only the first frame back over the original GIF, corrupting it

There are two self.downsize method definitions where the latter overrides the former and changes the signature, which will raise ArgumentError for callers still passing max_width, max_height (e.g. app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb)

After in-place downsize, ImageOptim replaces file by rename, causing tempfile.size (fstat on old fd) to go stale, resulting in all 5 passes running and Upload.create_for receiving stale filesize, dimensions and mismatched sha1
Downsizing animated GIFs with '80%' fails because gifsicle --resize-fit requires WxH geometry, not a percentage
Line 72 passes wrong size to Upload.create_for because tempfile.size reflects original file size, not downsized size - should use File.size(tempfile.path)
ResizeEmoji job calls OptimizedImage.downsize with 5 args against an arity of 3..4, causing every custom emoji resize to fail in Sidekiq
Duplicate method definition of downsize in OptimizedImage shadows the first version - Ruby does not support method overloading, so the second definition completely shadows the first
Hardcoding maxSizeKB to 10MB ignores the per-type max_*_size_kb site settings, so the client can accept files the server rejects or reject files when admins allow >10MB
tempfile && and tempfile.size > 0 checks in the new guard are redundant since loop condition already handles empty file and nil tempfile crashes later anyway
Error message in displayErrorForUpload on line 246 shows hardcoded 10MB instead of the actual configured limit, misleading users when server rejects files for exceeding smaller configured limits
HTTP 413 handler always tells user the limit is 10240 KB, but actual limit depends on nginx/proxy configuration which may differ
Switch case declaration in case 413 declares variable maxSizeKB without a block, allowing other cases to erroneously access the declaration - needs to be wrapped in a block for scope safety
Oversized SVGs enter the downsize loop because FileHelper.is_image? matches .svg, causing ImageMagick to rewrite user's SVG in place with re-encoded output
Upload validation hardcodes 10 MB and ignores the configured image/attachment size limits from Discourse.SiteSettings

Ruby's second def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) at line 149 silently overrides the first def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) at line 145, causing existing caller ResizeEmoji at resize_emoji.rb:14 to raise ArgumentError when calling with 5 arguments

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Client-side size check replaces SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb'] with hardcoded 10*1024 for all upload types, allowing attachments between max_attachment_size_kb and 10 MB to pass client check but fail server validation
The allow_animation option is effectively dead code since animated GIF downsizing fails through both upload paths
Sites with image limits above 10240 KB are now incorrectly capped in the browser due to hardcoded value
Inline rescue nil swallows all exceptions silently including network errors that might be worth logging

The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
Sites with upload limits above 10240 KB are incorrectly capped by the hardcoded client-side limit that admins never configured
For API URL uploads where .gif extension is preserved, gifsicle is triggered but --resize-fit 80% is invalid syntax (gifsicle requires WxH pixel dimensions, not percentages), causing silent failure
For regular browser uploads, Rack tempfile paths lack .gif extension, so the GIF detection regex in optimize() never matches and convert with [0] strips animation from GIFs
self.downsize is defined twice, with the second 4-arity definition silently replacing the 5-arity one, causing ArgumentError when callers pass width and height arguments

issues.claim: `self.downsize` is defined twice in OptimizedImage. Ruby has no overloading, so the later (from, to, dimensions, opts) definition replaces the (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) one, and existing 5-argument callers such as ResizeEmoji (app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14) raise ArgumentError.

API URL-based uploads now call FileHelper.download with a hardcoded 10.megabytes cap instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. This ignores the configured limit: larger files are truncated or blocked on sites allowing more than 10 MB, and more than allowed is downloaded on sites with smaller limits.

Client-side upload validation hardcodes maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 for all upload types instead of using Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']. Files the server will reject can pass the browser check, and files that sites configured above 10 MB allow are blocked.
The same 10 MB constant is duplicated in several places, so the client and server limits can drift apart.
The HTTP 413 handler always reports a limit of 10240 KB, although the actual limit depends on the nginx/proxy client_max_body_size setting.
The error message in displayErrorForUpload (line 246) shows a hardcoded 10 MB instead of the actual configured limit when the server rejects a file for exceeding a smaller configured limit.
In the switch statement, `case 413` declares `maxSizeKB` without a surrounding block, so the declaration is visible to the other cases.

The downsize loop reads `tempfile.size`, which stays stale after the in-place downsize and ImageOptim rename. As a result, the loop may run all passes or fail to terminate correctly, and Upload.create_for receives a stale filesize, dimensions and a mismatched sha1.
Downsizing passes '80%' as the dimensions. For animated GIFs this goes to `gifsicle --resize-fit`, which accepts only WxH pixel geometry, so gifsicle fails and every retry attempt is used up.
The allow_animation option is effectively dead code, because animated GIF downsizing fails through both upload paths.
Each upload can trigger up to 5 sequential ImageMagick plus ImageOptim runs on files up to 10 MB.
When OptimizedImage.downsize fails and returns false, the loop ignores the result, keeps retrying, and lets the oversized file continue.
The downsize loop shrinks the image to only about 33% of the original after 5 iterations (0.8^5), so an image can still exceed max_image_size_kb and proceed to Upload.create_for.
Non-API uploads run in the shared Scheduler::Defer.later queue, so large uploads stall unrelated deferred work.
No tests cover the new downsize loop, the changed OptimizedImage.downsize/optimize signatures, or the client validation change.
Image processing uses the same path for input and output, so the original file is lost if the operation fails mid-write.
With allow_animated_thumbnails off, `convert file[0]` writes only the first frame back over the original GIF.
For regular browser uploads, Rack tempfile paths lack a .gif extension, so the GIF detection regex in optimize() never matches and `convert` with [0] strips animation from GIFs.
The `tempfile &&` and `tempfile.size > 0` checks in the new guard are redundant with the loop condition and the later handling of a nil tempfile.
FileHelper.is_image? matches .svg, so oversized SVGs enter the downsize loop and ImageMagick rewrites the user's SVG in place.
An inline `rescue nil` silently swallows all exceptions, including network errors.
